I think the option for world authors to upload a few extra screenshots would go a surprisingly long way on helping with this issue.

Authors of high effort worlds that want to attract visitors and ensure their world isn't missed, are quite likely to take a minute to include extra screen shots to show it off.

Authors of low effort or otherwise basic worlds that hope to trick users into visiting, will either be forced to show the actual world with those screenshots, or won't be able to provide any. If they choose to use additional fake images then that will generally be much easier to notice, and would highlight the deception as being fully deliberate. Worlds that refuse to upload any addition shots despite having an amazing looking thumbnail, would be less trusted and less viral as a result.

Just this alone without even needing any ratings or active moderation, could likely solve the majority of the issue.

@{5b348634f5643c23501638a1|full_name} ohhhh this is an incredibly lovely idea, if I got a chance to see more photos of a world that it's author was able to provide, it would make world searching definitely more easy I feel!

A thing that another platform got right here was Sansar, they had a rule for thumbnails that at least 80% of a thumbnail had to show the actual world, the other 20% could be a text or a logo.

So people would not be coerced into a visit with a fake graphics or highly polished renders that did not represent the world at all.
@{6a364c54f51f79a5dbdc9b97|full_name} That would be great! Like a scrolling function that has a few images in-world to give a better idea of what you're going into. Love this.
I really am so tired of those trash worlds that trick you with a nice  or cool picture only to go in and it's the most awful half baked world ever. Please make this a thing!
That could be fixed really easily by having a full review system or like and dislike system.

Fancy looking AI image is not more misleading then fancy looking hand made art or photoshoped polished screenshots, which been in use in VRC world promotion for long time. Not to mention you got ton of meme worlds that whole point is misleading thumbnail. I think it would be hard to moderate that because it easy to disappoint people even if screenshot is legit.

Option to add extra more unedited screenshots may be best compromise here.

There also factor of worlds that look good on PC but not so shiny on Quest/Android due to hardware limitations regardless of having legit thumbnail from PC

@{5ae4f9f6801fa451b10edafc|full_name} They could add a report simply for a deceptive thumbnail. It would be pretty easy to filter the data from reports like that to determine if something is actually deceptive.

But yes, a fancy looking AI image that is basically just a screenshot of the world ran though an AI *is* deceiving. Usually, most images are clearly photoshopped (especially with text) or are a literal picture from the world itself.

@{5b348634f5643c23501638a1|full_name} I agree with this point. When you browse the Android/Google Play store for example, you can see screenshots of the app. I think requiring extra screenshots to have been taken from a camera in the world scene and incorporating that directly into the VRCSdk Uploader directly would give better results. 

Since there are ways to circumvent the system by like, pointing a camera at a static image, there needs to be clear TOS about what's acceptable. When someone clearly doctors an image meant to be representational "of actual game play" that should be a TOS violation and be flagged. That needs community driven feedback, which VRC doesn't really have right now except for "report".

@{645eeda6e453720915a7dc84|full_name}  No, it's an issue that is MUCH WORSE now because of AI, so it is indeed an AI issue too, because it lowered the barrier for deception.

The issue of the thumbnail not always showing the actual world and there being no other images is a long-standing issues though, yes. But most of the time the thumbnail was not trying to present itself as an image of the actual world, while these AI grifts are.

details:
# Issue

With the raise of AI there's a growing issue that's hard to go unnoticed - many worlds that use AI image generation (but not just them) for their thumbnails, often mislead their users about their actual content (with the focus on quality) of the world. As a world explorer the problem is impossible to ignore at this point and increasingly annoying. I'm not talking about having to perfectly represent or show the exact photo of the content of the world in the thumbnail - a stylized or somewhat responsibly reimagined representation is ok - but the thumbnails should not mislead you into believing that this is what you will get that would leave you disappointed. I'm talking thumbnails that make you believe that it's an actual in-world photo e.g. showing you a breathtaking high detailed beach but upon enter it's a sand and water planes with low poly palms.

# Platform moderation

The obvious issue is defining where the line is and the pure subjectivity of it. With moderation it'd be easy to go overboard and severely limit the freedom of world thumbnails and it would also greatly increase the work for the T&S team. There's a certain creativity with the relationship between the world page and the actual world. The obvious cases where someone is consciously and maliciously misleading you about the world's content or outright trolling you should be moderated tho.

# Community judgement

Best idea would be to offload this judgement to the users e.g. in the form of already suggested world voting. A world that gives you high hopes but leaves you disappointed would be represented by the community vote.

# Worlds tab & algorithms

Right now I feel like these "trap" worlds especially gain traction because once they pass a certain threshold they will end up in the "New & Noteworthy" tab and will pretty much get stuck there and have their "baitness" amplified even more. The Worlds tab algorithms are just something to consider too in the process of tackling this issue somehow.

# Better representation

Another idea would be to allow multiple photos of the world and e.g. have the game automatically take an extra photo of the world or allow the author to replace with one that MUST be originating from within the world.

# Final though

This is not exactly a specific feature request, nor duplication of the already existing "Add world voting" tickets, but casting limelight to the - I believe - increasingly visible problem that affects the quality of the platform and the joy of world exploration.
title: Tackle the misleading world thumbnails issue
